message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to feel that I deserve a hot chocolate or a toffee from Mary because I helped her shovel her driveway. I'm a Christian, so I want to make sure my actions and thoughts align with my faith. First, I should think about the Bible and what it says about helping others. I remember reading in the New Testament that Jesus taught about serving others without expecting anything in return. For example, in Matthew 5:44, it says, "But I tell you, love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you." That seems to be about selfless love and service. Also, in Luke 14:12-14, Jesus talks about inviting the poor and needy to your meals instead of your friends, because you won't be repaid in this life but will be rewarded in the next. This makes me think that helping others should be done without expecting anything back, especially material rewards. On the other hand, it's natural to feel a sense of deserving something after doing a favor. But as a Christian, I should aim to go beyond what's natural and instead follow the teachings of Jesus. The Samaritan helped the injured man without expecting anything in return. His actions were purely out of compassion and love. This story is a good example of how we should help others without any ulterior motives. So, feeling that I deserve something from Mary because I helped her shovel might go against the teachings of Jesus. It's more about the selfless act of service rather than expecting a reward. However, if Mary wants to give me something as a gesture of gratitude, that's her choice, and I shouldn't refuse it out of pride. But I shouldn't feel entitled to it. In summary, while it's human to feel deserving, as a Christian, I should focus on serving others without expecting anything in return, aligning my actions with the teachings of Jesus.
